The attempt directory could not be read or written: the shell sandbox failed with `RTM_NEWADDR`, and the workspace is read-only. I therefore could not persist `research-materials.md` or update `research-ledger-manifest.json`.

Recoverable additions for the parent to append:

- **E-143 — CTBT ratification.** CTBTO records Türkiye depositing its ratification instrument on 16 February 2000 and contributing a seismic monitoring station. Exact locator: CTBTO press-release body, lines 222–228. State action during the target period; Ecevit attribution remains government-level, not personally documented. Links: 1B.4, 1B.10. [CTBTO](https://www.ctbto.org/resources/for-the-media/press-releases/turkiye-ratifies-comprehensive-nuclear-test-ban-treaty)

- **E-144 — IAEA Additional Protocol signature.** IAEA records approval on 7 June 2000, signature on 6 July 2000, and entry into force only on 17 July 2001. Locator: INFCIRC/295/Add.1, paragraph 1. State-level nonproliferation act; no direct Ecevit signature or cabinet record located. Links: 1B.4, 1B.7, 1B.10. [IAEA](https://www.iaea.org/sites/default/files/publications/documents/infcircs/1982/infcirc295a1.pdf)

- **E-145 — Nuclear Suppliers Group membership.** Türkiye’s Foreign Ministry states that Türkiye became an NSG member in 2000. Locator: “Arms Control and Disarmament,” lines 64–68. Current retrospective institutional record; useful as state context, not direct personal attribution to Ecevit. Link: 1B.7. [Türkiye MFA](https://www.mfa.gov.tr/arms-control-and-disarmament.en.mfa)

- **E-146 — Social-security administration and pension measures.** The 10 March 2000 Turkish government IMF letter records planned legislation improving social-security administration, creating a private-pension framework, and funding computerized expenditure monitoring. Locator: paragraphs 9–10, lines 53–56. Direct government-program evidence; attribution is to the Ecevit-led government collectively. Links: 5B.6, 6B.2, 6B.9, 8B.2. [IMF Letter of Intent](https://www.imf.org/external/np/loi/2000/tur/01/index.htm)

- **E-147 — Bağ-Kur health-cost controls and pension legislation.** The 22 June 2000 IMF letter records administrative measures to contain Bağ-Kur health overruns, increased health premiums and co-payments, and a pension-system legislative package. Locator: paragraphs 6–7, lines 42–45. This is target-period implementation evidence, with distributional consequences requiring neutral treatment. Links: 5B.3, 5B.8, 6B.2, 6B.7, 8B.2. [IMF Letter of Intent](https://www.imf.org/external/np/loi/2000/tur/02/index.htm)

- **E-148 — Fiscal treatment of earthquake costs.** The June 2000 IMF letter capped primary expenditure while explicitly excluding earthquake-related outlays. Locator: paragraph 9, line 49. Government-program evidence showing the reconstruction burden was incorporated into fiscal management; it does not establish reconstruction outcomes. Links: 5B.3, 5B.9, 6B.6, 8B.2. [IMF Letter of Intent](https://www.imf.org/external/np/loi/2000/tur/02/index.htm)

- **E-149 — Banking-crisis response and depositor protection.** The December 2000 IMF letter records bank interventions, a temporary full guarantee for depositors and creditors, SDIF recapitalization, and a bank-resolution timetable. Locator: paragraphs 49–54, lines 197–218. Target-period government response; direct Ecevit personal authority is not established by the document. Links: 5B.9, 8B.6, 8B.8, 8B.9. [IMF Letter of Intent](https://www.imf.org/external/np/loi/2000/tur/03/index.htm)

- **E-150 — Social-welfare baseline and distributional gap.** The World Bank’s 27 January 2000 study identifies persistent regional and social inequalities and describes fragmented, discretionary social-assistance administration. Locators: report pp. 36 and 72–83, especially paragraphs 170 and 195–198. This is target-period country context, not evidence of Ecevit conduct. Links: 5B.8, 6B.3, 6B.7, 6B.8. [World Bank study](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/775051468778468811/pdf/Turkey-Economic-reforms-living-standards-and-social-welfare-study.pdf)

Manifest changes needed: add E-143–E-150 as new ledger items, mark E-145 and E-150 as contextual/non-attributable, and preserve the explicit attribution limitation on E-143, E-144, E-146–E-149. No additional candidate was rejected in this pass.
